core.title: Prove every admissible interlocking route with an e2e test
core.given: An interlocking plan artifact declares its guarded route space of admissible routes
core.when: a declared route has no e2e test exercising it
core.then: Write an e2e test that drives the route's guard-true inputs through the production route resolver, asserts the declared train was selected before execution, then executes that train through the production train executor.
prefer: Read the route, its guard and the train it resolves to; choose guard-true inputs that distinguish it from alternative routes.
Place the test where the stack's e2e layout puts interlocking route tests.
Drive the production route resolver with those inputs; pass the selected train to the production train executor and execute it.
Also assert the route- or acceptance-specific execution outcome when one is declared.
avoid: A route/train identifier literal added only so lexical coverage sees it.
A mock resolver or hand-built substitute for production route control.
A descriptive assertion restating the plan without exercising resolution.
Bypassing the production train executor after proving only selection.
unless: The plan artifact declares no route space (registry index, generated projections).
The route is already referenced by its route identifier or resolved train identifier in an e2e test: not flagged, though a token-only test still fails review.
The e2e rendering belongs to another stack's own realization of this obligation.
core.why: Each route is a production route-control branch; unexercised, it is a silent-green gap, and a bare token passes discovery while proving nothing. Strict: an admissible route without a covering e2e test blocks.
evidence: The coverage check finds, for every declared route, at least one e2e test referencing its route identifier or resolved train identifier outside comments.
Reviewer confirms the case would fail if the route guard or route-to-train mapping regressed.
Reviewer confirms the production route resolver and train executor actually execute the selected path, and that selection of the declared train is asserted before the train is executed.
Reviewer confirms the discoverable route/train token corresponds to behavior the case genuinely proves.
verification: The coverage check parses each interlocking plan artifact under the stack's interlocking scope, extracts its declared routes (route identifier, resolved train, category, guard reference), and scans the stack's e2e tests for references to each route by its route identifier or its resolved train identifier; references inside comments are masked and do not count.

The concrete serialization of the route space and of its route fields (route identifier, resolved train, category, guard reference) is the stack's plan syntax, supplied as profile data: the check consumes whatever the stack's interlocking plan artifacts declare; this core fixes no field names.

A route counts as covered when at least one e2e test references its route identifier or resolved train identifier outside comments; that token is a discovery proxy, not the testing objective — the check does not judge whether a referencing test genuinely proves the route (that is the review judgment).
Any declared route with no covering e2e test is flagged, anchored at the route's declaration in the interlocking plan artifact that declares it.

Plan artifacts under the interlocking scope that declare no route space (registry index, generated projections) carry no admissible route space and are skipped; the exact classification of such files is owned by this rule's checker.
Per-stack discovery — which e2e layout is scanned and which tokens establish reference — is delegated to each stack's realization; other stacks render the same obligation in their own e2e layout.
Severity 1, disposition strict: the rule blocks on every finding — an admissible route with no covering e2e test blocks.

Terms: admissible_route = a single declared route entry of an interlocking plan artifact's guarded route space, carrying its route identifier, the train it resolves to, a category and a guard reference; the interlocking plan artifact is authoritative for the guarded route space, and the production route resolver resolves each route to exactly one train. silent_green_route_gap = an admissible route with no covering e2e test; its route-control branch is never executed, so CI passes while a guarded route-control path is entirely unproven.

values: e2e route test added, changed or removed
declared interlocking route with no covering e2e test
test genuinely exercises route behavior rather than only containing a token
existing proof still proves the changed route

fires: A new route is added to an interlocking plan artifact's route space and no e2e test references its route identifier or resolved train identifier.
A route's guard or train mapping changes and its existing e2e proof is absent or no longer proves the changed route (its guard-true inputs or asserted train no longer match).
The coverage check reports a declared route with no covering e2e test.
A covering e2e test is deleted, leaving a declared route uncovered.
A route's or train's identifier appears in an e2e test only inside a comment: comments are masked and do not establish coverage, so the route is still uncovered.
doesNotFire: Plan artifacts under the interlocking scope that declare no route space (registry index, generated projections).
A route already referenced by its route identifier or resolved train identifier in an e2e test whose proof still exercises the route (not flagged by the check).
A route guard or train-mapping change whose existing e2e proof still drives and asserts the changed route correctly.
Another stack's e2e rendering of this obligation, which is owned by that stack's own realization.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the interlocking plan artifacts that declare the guarded route space live.
The plan-artifact kind that declares the guarded route space.
How an interlocking plan artifact declares its guarded route space (the list of admissible routes); the presence or absence of this construct decides whether the artifact carries route space at all.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `routes:` — the routes list of an interlocking YAML; every entry under `routes:` is an admissible route, and a file with no `routes:` key carries no admissible route space

profileRequirements.meaning: The plan-artifact field carrying a declared route's identifier (the core's 'route identifier').
The plan-artifact field carrying the train a declared route resolves to (the core's 'resolved train identifier').
profileRequirements.bunValue: trainId (the resolved trainId of the route)

profileRequirements.meaning: The plan-artifact field carrying the declared route's category.
The plan-artifact field referencing the declared route's guard.
Where the e2e tests scanned for route/train references live.
Where an e2e proof of one interlocking route is placed.
The stack's local name and entry point for the core's 'production route resolver': the component that resolves a declared route to exactly one train.
profileRequirements.bunValue: InterlockingRunner — `new InterlockingRunner(...).resolveTrain(action, inputs)` resolves a route to exactly one trainId

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's local name for the core's 'production train executor': the component that executes the train the resolver selected.
profileRequirements.bunValue: TrainRunner — receives the train the InterlockingRunner selected and executes it

neutralityNotes: The declared guarded route space is described semantically in the core; its concrete serialization (`routes:` of an interlocking YAML) and the route fields (routeId, trainId, category, guard_ref) are per-stack plan syntax carried by idiom.plan_syntax entries, and verification states that the check consumes the stack's plan syntax rather than fixed field names. The production runners have no neutral name in the closed vocabulary, so the core speaks of the production route resolver and train executor, mapped per stack by roles.runtime_components entries (Bun: InterlockingRunner with resolveTrain, and TrainRunner). The original Bun activation task terms (interlocking, route, routeId, trainId, InterlockingRunner, TrainRunner) are reconstructed exactly: the plan-field terms by idiom.plan_syntax#route_id/#train_id, the runner names by roles.runtime_components#route_resolver/#train_executor, plus a verbatim realization-level activation entry in bunOnly. Comment masking is kept as 'outside comments' without a profile key because bun.json states no concrete comment marker. Detector/validator/finding ids, the RAW-violation stage, the Bun language/runtime fact and the concrete skipped plan-tree files are bunOnly; per-rule severity 1 / strict disposition and the checker-owned exclusion deference live in core:verification, not in the profile. The distinction between a discoverable token and a genuine proof remains an llm_judged review judgment in every stack.
